# vphone-cli Run a virtual iPhone on an Apple Silicon Mac. > [!WARNING] > This project has never issued or authorized any cryptocurrency or token, and does not accept cryptocurrency payments or donations. Any cryptocurrency or token issued or promoted in this project's name, or claiming any affiliation with it, is a scam. vphone-cli runs iOS with Apple's Virtualization.framework and PCC research virtual machines, for security research, reverse engineering, and debugging. - **Graphical Window:** Use the virtual iPhone's screen on your Mac, browse apps and files, and take screenshots and screen recordings. - **Custom Firmware:** The system comes pre-patched, and you can install a package environment. - **Backup and Cloning:** You can export, import, and clone VMs. - **Automation API:** An optional local HTTP and WebSocket interface. - **No Extra Dependencies:** Needs no Xcode, Python, or Homebrew at runtime. ## Requirements - A physical Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or newer. It does not work in a macOS VM. - Free disk space. Each VM has a 64 GB virtual disk by default, and firmware takes more. - A network connection. Restoring the system fetches signing tickets online. - Adjusted security settings. Boot into macOS Recovery, run these commands in Terminal, then restart: ```sh csrutil enable --without debug csrutil allow-research-guests enable ``` SIP stays enabled, with only the debugging restrictions relaxed. For details, see [Host Setup](Documents/Guides/host-setup.md). ## Get Started 1. Download `vphone-launchpad--notarized.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/latest), unzip it, and open it. Not every release is notarized. If the latest one has no `-notarized` file, pick a notarized version from [Downloads](Documents/Downloads/README.md). 2. In **Host Setup**, grant Developer Tools access and install the helper. 3. In **Core Bundle**, click **Download and Install**. 4. In **Machines**, click **New Machine**, choose a firmware pairing, and click **Create**. Launchpad downloads the firmware, patches it, restores the system, and boots the VM. To use your own iPhone and cloudOS IPSWs, see [Compatibility](Documents/Guides/compatibility.md). To install a package manager in the VM, see [Package Environment](Documents/Guides/package-environment.md). ### Let an agent do it If you use a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) on this Mac, paste the prompt below instead of following the steps by hand. The agent reads the vphone skill, checks what is already set up, installs Launchpad and `VPhone.bundle`, and stops to ask when a step needs you, such as an administrator password or a change in macOS Recovery. ```text Set up vphone on this Mac. Read the skill at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/main/Skills/vphone-guest-control/SKILL.md and the files it links under references/ (same folder), then follow them: install the newest notarized vphone-launchpad (not every release has a -notarized zip), put vphone-launchpad-cli on PATH, install the VPhone.bundle that matches Launchpad's series, and check `vphone-launchpad-cli status`. Do not change SIP, boot-args or any other host security setting, and do not create a machine until I confirm the firmware and the free disk space. When a step needs me, tell me exactly what to do and wait. ``` ## Command Line Launchpad drives VMs through the `vphone-cli` inside `VPhone.bundle`. You can also run it in Terminal: ```sh vphone-cli vm list vphone-cli vm launch myphone vphone-cli vm export myphone --out myphone.tzst ``` VMs are stored in `~/.vphone/`. Run `vphone-cli --help` to see all commands. To create a VM without Launchpad, see [Create and Run](Documents/Guides/create-and-run.md). To turn on the automation API, add `--api-listen 127.0.0.1:8765` at launch and use the token it prints. See the [API documentation](Research/vphoned_http_api.md). ## Boot ROMs New VMs start from two open-source ROMs instead of the closed ones in Virtualization.framework: - [OpenAVB](https://github.com/owngoal-dev/OpenAVB) replaces AVPBooter, the boot ROM. It needs no patch, so `fw patch` leaves it alone. - [OpenSEP](https://github.com/owngoal-dev/OpenSEP) replaces AVPSEPBooter, the SEP boot ROM. With both, nothing Apple wrote runs before iBoot and SEPOS. Both ship in `VPhone.bundle`, prebuilt from pinned upstream commits. Each one's README ([OpenAVB](VPhoneExecutable/VPhoneVirtualization/Resources/OpenAVB/README.md), [OpenSEP](VPhoneExecutable/VPhoneVirtualization/Resources/OpenSEP/README.md)) says how to rebuild it and check it byte for byte. VMs created by earlier versions keep Apple's ROMs. A VM switches either way without a restore, from its next start: ```sh vphone-cli vm config myphone --rom openavb --seprom opensep # open-source ROMs vphone-cli vm config myphone --rom apple --seprom apple # Apple's ROMs ``` `vphone-cli vm info myphone` shows which ROMs a VM uses. Restoring a VM that boots OpenAVB needs `VPhone.bundle` 2.10.1 or newer. For the details, see [OpenAVB](Research/Firmware/openavb_boot_rom.md) and [OpenSEP](Research/Firmware/opensep_sep_rom.md) in the research notes. ## Documentation | Document | Contents | | --- | --- | | [Downloads](Documents/Downloads/README.md) | Notarized Launchpad versions and matching `VPhone.bundle` versions | | [Host Setup](Documents/Guides/host-setup.md) | SIP and AMFI settings, building from source, environment checks | | [Create and Run](Documents/Guides/create-and-run.md) | Firmware sources, the creation process, storage and backups | | [Snapshots](Documents/Guides/snapshots.md) | Save a stopped VM's disk state and revert to it | | [Compatibility](Documents/Guides/compatibility.md) | Verified firmware pairings | | [iPadOS Guests](Documents/Guides/ipados.md) | Run iPadOS (iPad mini A17 Pro) instead of iOS | | [Package Environment](Documents/Guides/package-environment.md) | Installing and removing a package manager in the VM | | [Troubleshooting](Documents/Guides/troubleshooting.md) | Common errors and how to fix them | | [Networking](Documents/Guides/networking.md) | Network modes, and `tunnel` for a Mac behind a VPN or proxy | | [Launchpad Command Line](Documents/Guides/launchpad-cli.md) | Install and test a local build with `vphone-launchpad-cli` | | [Contributing](Documents/README.md#for-contributors) | Project structure, building from source, research notes | If these do not solve your problem, [open an issue](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/issues). ## Acknowledgements - [wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup](https://github.com/wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup) - [owngoal-dev/OpenAVB](https://github.com/owngoal-dev/OpenAVB) and [owngoal-dev/OpenSEP](https://github.com/owngoal-dev/OpenSEP), the boot ROMs new VMs start from

## vphone 2.13.1

**Core Bundle**
- `fw patch`'s filesystem step no longer stops after sealing with "“new.trustcache” couldn’t be moved to “Firmware” because an item with the same name already exists". The new trust cache is already written into `Firmware`, and the manifest rewrite moved it onto itself, which FileManager refuses on the macOS 27 host it was seen on.

**Launchpad 2.13.1**
- No changes besides the version. Same 2.13 series: Launchpad 2.13.1 works with Core Bundle 2.13.x, and Launchpad 2.13.0 works with Core Bundle 2.13.1. The helper is unchanged (build 21).
- `vphone-launchpad-2.13.1.zip` is built by CI and not notarized; macOS blocks it the first time you open it (see [Downloads](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/blob/main/Documents/Downloads/README.md)). `vphone-launchpad-2.13.0-notarized.zip` keeps working with this bundle.

**Upgrading**

In Launchpad's Core Bundle page, install `VPhone.bundle` 2.13.1. Existing machines keep their Core Bundle bindings until you change them.

**Validation**

- A Debug build of the `VPhone` scheme succeeded, bundle admission included. The failing `moveItem` was reproduced on its own on macOS 27.

releases.name: vphone 2.12.2
releases.body:
## vphone 2.12.2

**Core Bundle**
- HomePod guests can mount tvOS developer disk images and install apps from Xcode: a scoped cryptexd compatibility layer (file protection, until-reboot DDI installation, the research SEP's missing digest storage), the tvOS Cryptex product class in the device tree with native signature, root-hash and trust-cache checks kept, and scoped UserManager lookup plus ad hoc signature support for app installation. The patches are version-gated, selected by `homepod-mini`, and reversible. Building an app needs a patched tvOS SDK and `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 3,5`. Thanks to @insidegui. (#731)
- HomePod controls: a click or click-and-hold near the centre of the display is a top cap tap or long press, a **User Defaults…** sheet edits SoundBoard's debugging defaults (search, typed editors, range checks, read-back on save, reset), and **Restart SoundBoard** applies the ones that need it. Thanks to @insidegui. (#734)
- `fw patch`'s filesystem step works again: it creates the mount point before `diskutil image attach`, and seals with the time of the first entry edited after encryption, the time the restore's own `mtree -m` derives, so `seal_system_volume` no longer

releases.name: vphone 2.12.1
releases.body:
## vphone 2.12.1

**Core Bundle**
- The research board's kernelcache mix is extracted natively: `fw kernelcache` no longer needs an `ipsw` built from unmerged branches (`--ipsw` and `VPHONE_IPSW` are accepted and ignored), and a mix linked by macOS 27's kmutil branches past the auth stubs it keeps, so the research-board guests boot when linked on macOS 27. Thanks to @0xJacky. (#729)
- Every guest family can be created on a macOS 26.6.2 host (#732):
  - watchOS and the iOS 18 (Minimal) guests merge and seal their restore image: the mount point is created before `diskutil image attach`, and a system image whose container already fills its file is grown before the seal.
  - The research-board flow no longer stops at "Operation not permitted" when an earlier sudo run created the IPSW cache.
  - iOS 18.7 and 18.7.2 restores no longer fail at "Unable to send data to ASR": a chunk the socket takes only part of is finished instead of corrupting the stream.
  - A template's setup boot applies its service profile again when launchd refuses a change this early in the boot.
- tvOS 27.0 and HomePod Software 27.2 need macOS 27: their OTAs are compressed with LZRAVEN, which only macOS 27 unpacks.

releases.name: vphone 2.12.0
releases.body:
## vphone 2.12.0

### Core Bundle and Launchpad

- Merge the full Minimal, research-board, Apple Watch, iOS 18 and iOS 26 contribution stack, preserving the original commits and authorship. Thanks to @mpass99. (#712, #713, #714, #716, #718, #720)
- Add the `minimal` preset, support cloudOS releases without vphone600 components, and support iOS 26.x and iOS 18.x guests with their matching research-board boot chains.
- Add Apple Watch guests (Watch7,18 / watchOS 26.4) and pairing with a virtual iPhone.
- Let NAT guests reach one another, with per-machine isolation controls and corrected fixed-address reporting. Hosts without the required isolation API fail safely. (#717)
- Keep privileged firmware operations inside private workspaces, reject untrusted native patch-set code when running as root, and confine kernel cache access and guest filesystem writes.
- Fix SSH transfers that could hang while writing input and collecting error output.
- Start the 2.12 compatibility series: use Launchpad 2.12.x with Core Bundle 2.12.x. Launchpad includes helper build 20; updating the helper may request administrator authorization.

vphone-cli

Run a virtual iPhone on an Apple Silicon Mac.

Warning

This project has never issued or authorized any cryptocurrency or token, and does not accept cryptocurrency payments or donations. Any cryptocurrency or token issued or promoted in this project's name, or claiming any affiliation with it, is a scam.

vphone-cli runs iOS with Apple's Virtualization.framework and PCC research virtual machines, for security research, reverse engineering, and debugging.

  • Graphical Window: Use the virtual iPhone's screen on your Mac, browse apps and files, and take screenshots and screen recordings.
  • Custom Firmware: The system comes pre-patched, and you can install a package environment.
  • Backup and Cloning: You can export, import, and clone VMs.
  • Automation API: An optional local HTTP and WebSocket interface.
  • No Extra Dependencies: Needs no Xcode, Python, or Homebrew at runtime.

Requirements

  • A physical Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or newer. It does not work in a macOS VM.

  • Free disk space. Each VM has a 64 GB virtual disk by default, and firmware takes more.

  • A network connection. Restoring the system fetches signing tickets online.

  • Adjusted security settings. Boot into macOS Recovery, run these commands in Terminal, then restart:

    csrutil enable --without debug
csrutil allow-research-guests enable

    SIP stays enabled, with only the debugging restrictions relaxed. For details, see Host Setup.

Get Started

  1. Download vphone-launchpad-<version>-notarized.zip from the latest release, unzip it, and open it. Not every release is notarized. If the latest one has no -notarized file, pick a notarized version from Downloads.
  2. In Host Setup, grant Developer Tools access and install the helper.
  3. In Core Bundle, click Download and Install.
  4. In Machines, click New Machine, choose a firmware pairing, and click Create.

Launchpad downloads the firmware, patches it, restores the system, and boots the VM. To use your own iPhone and cloudOS IPSWs, see Compatibility.

To install a package manager in the VM, see Package Environment.

Let an agent do it

If you use a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) on this Mac, paste the prompt below instead of following the steps by hand. The agent reads the vphone skill, checks what is already set up, installs Launchpad and VPhone.bundle, and stops to ask when a step needs you, such as an administrator password or a change in macOS Recovery.

Set up vphone on this Mac. Read the skill at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/main/Skills/vphone-guest-control/SKILL.md
and the files it links under references/ (same folder), then follow them:
install the newest notarized vphone-launchpad (not every release has a
-notarized zip), put vphone-launchpad-cli on PATH, install the VPhone.bundle
that matches Launchpad's series, and check `vphone-launchpad-cli status`.
Do not change SIP, boot-args or any other host security setting, and do not
create a machine until I confirm the firmware and the free disk space. When a
step needs me, tell me exactly what to do and wait.

Command Line

Launchpad drives VMs through the vphone-cli inside VPhone.bundle. You can also run it in Terminal:

vphone-cli vm list
vphone-cli vm launch myphone
vphone-cli vm export myphone --out myphone.tzst

VMs are stored in ~/.vphone/. Run vphone-cli <group> --help to see all commands. To create a VM without Launchpad, see Create and Run.

To turn on the automation API, add --api-listen 127.0.0.1:8765 at launch and use the token it prints. See the API documentation.

Boot ROMs

New VMs start from two open-source ROMs instead of the closed ones in Virtualization.framework:

  • OpenAVB replaces AVPBooter, the boot ROM. It needs no patch, so fw patch leaves it alone.
  • OpenSEP replaces AVPSEPBooter, the SEP boot ROM.

With both, nothing Apple wrote runs before iBoot and SEPOS. Both ship in VPhone.bundle, prebuilt from pinned upstream commits. Each one's README (OpenAVB, OpenSEP) says how to rebuild it and check it byte for byte.

VMs created by earlier versions keep Apple's ROMs. A VM switches either way without a restore, from its next start:

vphone-cli vm config myphone --rom openavb --seprom opensep   # open-source ROMs
vphone-cli vm config myphone --rom apple --seprom apple       # Apple's ROMs

vphone-cli vm info myphone shows which ROMs a VM uses. Restoring a VM that boots OpenAVB needs VPhone.bundle 2.10.1 or newer. For the details, see OpenAVB and OpenSEP in the research notes.

Documentation

Document Contents
Downloads Notarized Launchpad versions and matching VPhone.bundle versions
Host Setup SIP and AMFI settings, building from source, environment checks
Create and Run Firmware sources, the creation process, storage and backups
Snapshots Save a stopped VM's disk state and revert to it
Compatibility Verified firmware pairings
iPadOS Guests Run iPadOS (iPad mini A17 Pro) instead of iOS
Package Environment Installing and removing a package manager in the VM
Troubleshooting Common errors and how to fix them
Networking Network modes, and tunnel for a Mac behind a VPN or proxy
Launchpad Command Line Install and test a local build with vphone-launchpad-cli
Contributing Project structure, building from source, research notes

If these do not solve your problem, open an issue.

Acknowledgements

  • wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup
  • owngoal-dev/OpenAVB and owngoal-dev/OpenSEP, the boot ROMs new VMs start from

aiSummary.oneLiner: A command-line tool for interacting with VirtualPhone, enabling automated management of virtual iOS devices.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: vphone-cli provides a terminal-based interface and automation toolkit for managing VirtualPhone instances (a platform for running virtualized iOS devices). It bridges the gap between the VirtualPhone GUI and automated CI/CD workflows by allowing developers to programmatically control device lifecycles. Users can use the CLI to create, start, stop, and snapshot virtual iPhones, as well as install applications, push files, and execute shell commands inside the virtual environment. This abstraction is critical for teams that need to integrate iOS testing, security analysis, or app deployment into headless scripts without relying on manual interaction.
keyFeatures: Device lifecycle management: Commands to boot, shutdown, and reset virtual iOS devices.
App installation: Sideload IPA files directly into the virtual environment from the command line.
File system interaction: Push and pull files between the host machine and the virtual device.
Snapshot control: Create and restore device states for reproducible testing scenarios.
Shell execution: Run commands directly within the virtual iOS environment.
CI/CD integration: Designed for headless operation within automated testing pipelines.

useCases.title: Automated iOS testing
useCases.description: QA engineers use the CLI in CI/CD pipelines to spin up a clean virtual iPhone, install a new build, and run tests.

useCases.title: Security research
useCases.description: Security analysts script the rapid deployment and teardown of specific iOS versions for vulnerability analysis.

useCases.title: App reverse engineering
useCases.description: Researchers use the tool to automate the extraction of app data and memory dumps from virtualized devices.

useCases.title: Headless device management
useCases.description: DevOps teams manage fleets of virtual iOS devices on remote servers without requiring graphical access.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This tool is built for iOS developers, QA automation engineers, and security researchers who need programmatic control over virtualized iOS environments. It requires access to VirtualPhone and familiarity with command-line interfaces.
